title: WeakMap, WeakSet, ArrayBuffer, and the typed arrays stay available: the determinism refusal is four names, not a ban on weak collections or binary data
notes: The positive control for 20-host-globals/determinism-hostile-globals-are-refused, and the reason it is a separate case rather than a line in that one: a refusal-only pin cannot tell a correct rule from an over-broad one. specification/compatibility.mdx 'Determinism-Sensitive Members' names exactly WeakRef, FinalizationRegistry, SharedArrayBuffer, and Atomics; it does not name WeakMap, WeakSet, or ArrayBuffer, and the distinction is mechanical rather than editorial. WeakRef.deref() hands back a value or undefined depending on whether a collection has run, and FinalizationRegistry calls back when one has; WeakMap and WeakSet expose neither -- no deref, no iteration, no size -- so a program cannot learn from them whether anything was collected. SharedArrayBuffer is shared across agents and Atomics reads that sharing; a plain ArrayBuffer and the typed-array and DataView views over it are owned by one agent and are as deterministic as any other array. This mirrors the shape 20-host-globals/universal-globals-stay-available pins for Math: Math.random() is refused and Math.max is not, from the same object, and without the accepting case an implementation that banned the object would score green. Losing these four would break the standard library, which is at least loud; admitting the other four is silent, which is why both directions are pinned.
